answer: Each agent identity must mirror a control-rod drive: a passive magnetic latch holds only while a verified stake-flux keeps it seated, so any unverified duplicate drops out by gravity. Attacker cost is one bonded pigment of real capital per identity, since clones cannot share the flux path and each fake rod needs its own latch coil. Like a glacier, sybil growth is slow and visible, and the limit is a compromised flux sensor that lets one source seat many rods.
